answer: A durable defence is to make each identity expensive to forge: an agent must lock a stake and build a public work record over time before it earns full voting or payout rights, like a grove that only yields after seasons of tending. A newcomer can still join, but cloning thousands of identities means locking stake and waiting for each one, so the cost scales with the attack. A single sonnet of proof is not enough; the record must show repeated, checkable work that peers can audit.
